textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · Exploring Magnets · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: A magnet attracts some materials, such as iron, nickel and cobalt. These are magnetic materials. Materials like wood, plastic, glass, paper and rubber are not attracted. They are non-magnetic.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A magnet attracts some materials, such as iron, nickel and cobalt. These are magnetic materials. Materials like wood, plastic, glass, paper and rubber are not attracted. They are non-magnetic.
beats.speakEn: A magnet attracts some materials, such as iron, nickel and cobalt. These are magnetic materials. Materials like wood, plastic, glass, paper and rubber are not attracted. They are non-magnetic.

beats.en: In a bar magnet, the pull is usually strongest near the two ends, called the poles. They are the north pole and the south pole. If we break a magnet, each piece still has two poles.
beats.speakEn: In a bar magnet, the pull is usually strongest near the two ends, called the poles. They are the north pole and the south pole. If we break a magnet, each piece still has two poles.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · Exploring Magnets · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Unlike poles attract each other. A north pole pulls a south pole. Like poles repel each other. Two north poles push apart.

beats.en: Unlike poles attract each other. A north pole pulls a south pole. Like poles repel each other. Two north poles push apart. In these classroom tests, repulsion by a known magnet is a sure sign of another magnet.
beats.speakEn: Unlike poles attract each other. A north pole pulls a south pole. Like poles repel each other. Two north poles push apart. In these classroom tests, repulsion by a known magnet is a sure sign of another magnet.

beats.en: A magnetic compass has a small magnetised needle that points north and south. We use a compass to find directions when we are lost or at sea.
beats.speakEn: A magnetic compass has a small magnetised needle that points north and south. We use a compass to find directions when we are lost or at sea.

type: Unlike poles attract each other. A north pole pulls a south pole. Like poles repel each other.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · Exploring Magnets · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: Magnets are used in fridge doors, speakers, toys, cranes and in separating iron from waste. Keep strong magnets away from magnetic-stripe cards and sensitive devices.
